headline: Revenue and orders climb; margins compress on rising costs
summary_short: GE HealthCare's Q2 FY2026 revenue was $5,294M (+5.8% y/y, +3.2% q/q), with net income of $560M (+15.2% y/y) and diluted EPS of $1.24 (+17.0% y/y), aided by IEEPA tariff refunds and a lower tax rate.
summary_long: Revenue of $5,294M (+5.8% y/y) was driven by Pharmaceutical Diagnostics (+15.6% reported) and Advanced Imaging Solutions (+7.9% reported), while Patient Care Solutions revenue fell 13.3% and stayed under pressure. Net income margin rose 90bp y/y to 10.6%, but Adjusted EBIT margin fell 40bp to 14.2% as PCS weakness and ~$250M of memory-chip/oil/freight inflation offset gains elsewhere. Diluted EPS of $1.24 (+17.0% y/y) and Adjusted EPS of $1.13 (+6.6%) both benefited from $129M of IEEPA tariff refunds and a lower tax rate. Orders grew a record 11.1% organically, book-to-bill 1.15x, backlog $23.9B. Cash and equivalents were $2.1B; the company reaffirmed FY2026 guidance (organic revenue growth 3.0-4.0%, Adjusted EPS $4.80-$5.00).

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by Pharmaceutical Diagnostics and Advanced Imaging Solutions, with strength in the U.S., EMEA, and Rest of World; Patient Care Solutions performance continued to be challenged.
Benefited from $129M of IEEPA tariff refunds and a lower tax rate versus the prior-year quarter.
Margin measures were negatively impacted by a decline in PCS and inflation related to memory chips, oil, and freight costs.
Grew on tariff refunds and a lower effective tax rate, per the same drivers cited for net income.
CEO cited record orders and backlog growth across every segment, though PCS remains under strategic review to restore growth and profitability.
